tara: Follow-up from the dedicated pool RFC bench. Two corner cases: noisy-tenant prewarm hoarding and rapid attach failures causing cascading scale retries.

tara: Bench profile: 55% tiny (<40 tokens), 30% medium, 15% long; 8 tenants did 70% of bursts. Short spikes lasted 8-12s.

miguel: For hoarding: tenant-level token-based credit with decay seems best. Also enforce a soft_max concurrency per tenant so they cant starve others.

jo: For attach failures: introduce a pool-level attach-window and circuit breaker that limits parallel attaches and backs off per failure.

sam: config sketch: autoscale_policy.min=1 max=250 headroom=0.16 prewarm.default_credits=3 prewarm.decay_mins=30 tenant.soft_max=12 pool.attach.max_parallel=3 pool.attach.cooldown=60s pool.circuit_breaker.fail_threshold=5

ops-bot: note: canary deployment scheduled for autoscaler-v2 at 14:00 UTC.

miguel: operator vs control-plane: operator should enforce local credits and attach limits. control-plane writes intent + audit log. That avoids flapping if API is slow.

jo: add telemetry: tenant_credit_level, attach_attempts, attach_failures, scale_intent_reason. Useful for postmortem.

tara: action items: tara -> RFC addendum w/ credit semantics (due Thu). miguel -> implement attach circuit breaker prototype (PR next Tue). jo -> dashboards + alerts (by next Fri). sam -> coordinate canary rollout and safety kill-switch.

ops-bot: canary started: autoscaler-v2 -> runtime-staging zone-b
